svg.text: Glugg on the 40×60 protoboard · step 2: wiring the underside
Board flipped over left-to-right: the +5 V strip stays at the top, and column A is now on the RIGHT.
Bare links (tinned wire or a bent component leg, soldered pad to pad)
A14 → A13: diode band to the H2's 5V pin
E14 → +5 V strip: diode's other end
N13 → N14 → +5 V strip: the S3's 5V pin
I12 → I13 → I14 → +5 V strip: chip pins 1 and 2 (unused) to +5 V
L11 → L12 → L13 → L14 → +5 V strip: chip pin 14 (VCC), 13 and 12
G12 → H12: H2 RX to the 1 kΩ
N12 → M12 → M11: S3 GND to the 100 nF and the 10 kΩ
I10 → I9 → J9 → J8 → J7 → I7: chip pins 4, 5 (unused) to pin 7 (GND)
L9 → L8 → M8: chip pins 10 and 9 (the inputs) to the 10 kΩ
L7 → M7: chip pin 8 (output) to the 330 Ω
P3 → Q3 → R3 → S3: 1000 µF + to the terminal's 5V
Insulated wires (solid core, strip 3 mm at each end)
red: R3 → +5 V strip (feeds the terminal and the 1000 µF)
black: H2 GND (A12) → GND strip, along column B
black: S3 GND (N12) → GND strip, along column O
black: chip pin 7 (I7) → GND strip, along column I
yellow: S3 GPIO13 (T11) → M8 (LED data in)
Insulated wires may cross each other. Bare links must never touch a neighbouring pad: look at each one with a magnifier before moving on.
